1.outline: Term theme: 'Data Modelling'. Recap SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN from earlier years, ready to build toward IF and lookups.
1.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, formula reference card.
objectives: Recall SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN formulas.
Apply all four to a sample dataset.
Explain what each formula calculates.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Formula recap
plan.detail: Apply SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN to a sample dataset, checking each result makes sense.

plan.title: Speed quiz
plan.detail: Quickfire: which formula would you use for this question? Pairs answer on whiteboards.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

activities: Apply four formulas to sample data
successCriteria: I correctly applied SUM, AVERAGE, MAX and MIN.
I chose the right formula for a given question.
I can explain what each formula calculates.

2.outline: Learn the =IF() function to make a cell display different results depending on a condition.
2.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, IF-function reference.
objectives: Write a basic =IF formula.
Explain the three parts of an IF formula: condition, true, false.
Test the formula with values on both sides of the condition.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: IF in real life
plan.detail: Everyday IF examples: IF it rains, take an umbrella, ELSE leave it home.

plan.title: Build an IF formula
plan.detail: Write =IF(B2>=50,"Pass","Fail") on sample scores. Test with scores above and below 50.

plan.title: Explain it
plan.detail: Explain the three parts of the formula to a partner. Save and log out.

activities: Build and test an IF formula
successCriteria: I wrote a working IF formula.
I can name the three parts of an IF formula.
I tested it with values on both sides of the condition.

3.outline: Learn the difference between a relative reference (changes when copied) and an absolute reference with $ signs (stays fixed).
3.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, references handout.
objectives: Explain the difference between relative and absolute references.
Use $ signs to lock a reference.
Fix a formula that broke because of the wrong reference type.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: The problem
plan.detail: Copy a formula down that references a fixed 'tax rate' cell — watch it break because the reference moved too.

plan.title: Lock it with $
plan.detail: Add $ signs to lock the tax-rate reference, then copy down again — now it works.

plan.title: Fix a broken one
plan.detail: Given a broken formula, fix it by adding the right $ signs. Save and log out.

activities: Watch a formula break when copied
successCriteria: I can explain relative vs absolute references.
I used $ signs to lock a reference correctly.
I fixed a broken formula caused by the wrong reference type.

4.outline: Start building a small spreadsheet model — a trip budget or event planner — with inputs the user can change.
4.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, model exemplar.
objectives: Plan a simple spreadsheet model.
Set up clearly labelled input cells.
Add formulas that calculate from those inputs.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Choose a model
plan.detail: Choose trip budget or event planner; sketch the inputs and outputs needed.

plan.title: Build the model
plan.detail: Set up labelled input cells and formulas that calculate totals from them.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My model has clearly labelled input cells.
My model calculates a total from those inputs.
My formulas use the correct reference type.

5.outline: Change an input value in the model and observe how the outputs update automatically — the core idea of 'what-if' analysis.
objectives: Change an input value and observe the effect.
Explain what 'what-if' means in a spreadsheet.
Record two different what-if scenarios.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What-if demo
plan.detail: Change one input in the model on the big screen and watch the output change instantly.

plan.title: Try two scenarios
plan.detail: Try two different what-if scenarios in your own model and record the results.

plan.title: Discuss
plan.detail: Which scenario gave a better outcome, and why? Save and log out.

successCriteria: I changed an input and saw the output update.
I can explain what 'what-if' means.
I recorded two scenario results.

6.outline: Add a chart to the model that presents the results clearly to someone who has not seen the raw numbers.
6.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, chart-choice poster.
objectives: Choose a suitable chart type for the model's results.
Add a titled, labelled chart.
Check the chart makes sense on its own.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Add a chart
plan.detail: Choose and insert a suitable chart type for the model's results, with a title and labels.

plan.title: Stand-alone test
plan.detail: Cover the numbers — does the chart alone still make sense? Adjust labels if not.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: My chart type suits the data.
My chart has a title and labels.
My chart makes sense without seeing the raw numbers.

7.outline: Write a short paragraph interpreting the model — what does it show, and what would you recommend based on it?
7.sowResources: Microsoft Word / Google Docs, writing frame.
objectives: Interpret what the model's results mean.
Write a short paragraph explaining the findings.
Make one recommendation based on the data.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: What does it show?
plan.detail: Discuss as a class: what story does the model's chart tell?

plan.title: Write it up
plan.detail: Write a short paragraph explaining the model's findings and one recommendation.

plan.title: Peer check
plan.detail: Partner checks the write-up matches the actual chart. Save and log out.

successCriteria: My paragraph explains what the model shows.
My paragraph includes one recommendation.
My write-up matches my actual chart.

8.outline: Finish and polish the portfolio piece: a spreadsheet model using IF, with a short explanation of one what-if result.
8.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, portfolio folder.
objectives: Finish the model with a working IF formula.
Ensure the chart and write-up are complete.
Save the finished piece to the portfolio folder.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Finish the model
plan.detail: Complete the model: IF formula, chart, and written interpretation all present.

plan.title: Rubric self-check
plan.detail: Check against the assessment rubric before saving.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save to the portfolio folder. Log out.

successCriteria: My model includes a working IF formula.
My model has a chart and a written interpretation.
My finished model is saved to the portfolio folder.

9.outline: Extend the model's write-up by adding and interpreting a second what-if scenario.
9.sowResources: Microsoft Excel, Google Sheets, Microsoft Word / Google Docs.
objectives: Run a second what-if scenario.
Compare it with the first scenario.
Add the comparison to the write-up.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Second scenario
plan.detail: Change the inputs again to run a second what-if scenario, recording the result.

plan.title: Compare and write
plan.detail: Add a sentence comparing the two scenarios to the write-up.

plan.title: Save
plan.detail: Save and log out.

successCriteria: I ran a second what-if scenario.
I compared it with the first scenario.
My write-up now covers both scenarios.

10.outline: Rehearse the term's modelling skills in pairs: build a formula, test a what-if, add a chart.
10.sowResources: Recap slide deck, practice task cards.
objectives: Recall the term's modelling process in order.
Rehearse building an IF formula and a chart with a partner.
Identify the trickiest step.

plan.title: TypingClub warm-up
plan.detail: 10 minutes, posture check.

plan.title: Process recap
plan.detail: Recap: inputs, formula, IF, chart, interpret — as a class chant.

plan.title: Paired rehearsal
plan.detail: Build a small IF-based model with a partner reading the task card, then swap.

plan.title: Tricky step check
plan.detail: Name the step you still find hardest. Log out.

successCriteria: I can list the term's modelling steps in order.
I rehearsed building a model with a partner.
I know which step needs more practice.

11.outline: Individual task: build a spreadsheet model using IF, then write a short explanation of one what-if result.
objectives: Build a spreadsheet model that calculates automatically.
Use an IF function correctly.
Present findings with a chart and a short explanation.

plan.title: Settle and explain
plan.detail: Calm start — explain the task and rubric.

plan.title: Build the model
plan.detail: Individual practical: given inputs, build a model with an IF formula and a chart.

plan.title: Write the explanation
plan.detail: Write a short explanation of one what-if result.

plan.title: Celebrate
plan.detail: Save and celebrate the term's progress. Log out.

successCriteria: My model calculates automatically from inputs.
I used an IF function correctly.
I explained one what-if result clearly.
